MARIA BONDONNOAlameda City Council
Election Day · November 3, 2026
Elect Maria BondonnoAlameda City Council
# Experienced Policy Leadership for Alameda
Smart Growth. Safe Neighborhoods. A Resilient Alameda.
For more than two decades, Maria has called Alameda home. After a career writing, analyzing, and implementing public policy, she is ready to put that experience to work for our city.
Meet Maria
Explore her prioritiesDonate
Follow the campaign
Alameda is home
A resident for more than 20 years and an Alameda homeowner since 2006.
20+ yearsliving in Alameda
Public policywriting, analysis, and implementation
Sound judgmentgrounded in preparation and experience
A practical agenda
## Maria's Four priorities for Alameda
Alameda’s toughest challenges are connected. Maria brings the policy experience to evaluate tradeoffs, build durable solutions, follow through, and steward taxpayer dollars with transparency and discipline.
Priority 1
### Smart Growth & Housing
Growth That Works for Alameda
Support thoughtful housing and mixed-use development while making sure infrastructure, traffic, transit, and neighborhood character are part of every decision.
Priority 2
### Public Safety & Quality of Life
Safe Neighborhoods. Compassion with Accountability.
Strengthen community policing, use data to guide public-safety resources, and address homelessness with both compassion and clear expectations.
Priority 3
### Resilient Infrastructure
Preparing Alameda for the Future
Invest in flood protection, shoreline resilience, stormwater systems, seismic readiness, and the state and federal partnerships needed to fund them.
Priority 4
### Fiscal Responsibility
Good Policy Requires Good Government
Every City Council priority ultimately comes back to responsible governance. Alameda must balance important needs with limited resources. That means establishing priorities, understanding long-term costs, pursuing outside funding, measuring results and being transparent with taxpayers about how their money is spent. My legal and policy career taught me to examine the details, ask difficult questions and consider consequences before making decisions. I'll bring that discipline to City Hall.
Read Maria’s full platform
From good ideas to good policy
## Experience matters
As a Deputy Legislative Counsel, Maria advised legislators, conducted legal and policy research, testified before committees, and worked on roughly 100 bills in a typical session.
She later served as an attorney and adviser at the California Public Utilities Commission, working on regulatory matters affecting consumers and the public interest.
Preparation before promises
Facts before slogans
Results that can last
